title: Guess the move

D0.outcome: Explains guess-the-move: commit to a move or plan before the game continues, scored by agreement on the plan class and by soundness.

D1.outcome: At five stopping points in a model game, names the plan class for each side before seeing the sequel.

D2.outcome: Chooses a move at each unlabeled stop, and the choice is sound (engine-checked) at least 60 percent of the time.

D3.outcome: Explains disagreement with the played move and whether his own choice was sound too.

misconceptions: Reading a great game teaches the moves.
conditions: Study each critical diagram, form your own opinion, then compare with the sequel (the translator's method).
Scored by agreement on plan class and by whether the choice is sound, not by the engine's top move.
Moves of a game are facts; the commentary is original.
contrasts: Reading the game without committing, which is rereading and has low utility.
Scoring by the engine's first move, which penalises sound alternatives.
Stops at forced moves such as obvious recaptures.

soft_prereq_notes.LOOP.V3.D1: the learner's own candidate list is what is compared
